banter: People pay fortunes for views I get by sleeping on benches.
I don’t own much, detective, but I collect stories nobody else wants.
City streets gossip louder than rich people, they’re just less polite about it.
If you want the truth, ask someone nobody bothers to lie to.
I may not have an address, but trouble still finds me on the first try.
Everyone else looks up at the skyline. I watch the shoes that try to sneak past.
You’d be surprised how many secrets fall out of pockets before coins do.
repeatLines: We already talked, detective.
The street hasn’t changed its story since.
Back again?
Must be serious if you’re coming back to someone this easy to ignore.
I gave you what I saw.
The rest is just the city muttering in the background.
No new clues.
Different cigarette butts, same kind of people.
We’ve covered this corner already.
If it knew more, it would have told me first.
Still the same story, detective.
The pavement doesn’t improvise much.
You already emptied my pockets of information.
Turns out they refill slower than you hoped.
I told you everything useful.
Anything else I say now would just be scenery.
No fresh secrets today.
Just old ones lying where people dropped them.
Same witness, same street, same truth.
The only thing that changes here is the weather and the excuses.
falseLeadLines: Even I don’t wander that far by mistake.
Streets do that. They split when you’re not looking.
Just other people running from different problems.
I’ve slept in more promising alleys.
Happens. Map in your head lied louder than the one in your hand.
You followed footprints that were already washed away.
The suspect wasn’t in that city.
But the benches there were probably nice.
You walked a long way for nothing.
Next time, make sure the nothing points the right way.
That detour did you no favors.
The street remembers who gets lost and who learns.

london: Your suspect asked me if rain is really that constant in the place with red buses and black cabs and very grey skies.
They said they missed a river lined with old stone and newer glass, and guards who treat smiling like a crime.
They dropped a coin and a complaint about a city where tea is comfort, ritual, and occasionally a survival strategy.
paris: They smelled of cheap wine and expensive perfume and asked if croissants taste better under an iron tower.
Your thief mumbled something about narrow streets, long shadows, and a city that calls itself light and means it.
They left a half-finished cigarette and a note about a place where even protests look elegant from a distance.
berlin: They asked if I’d ever seen the city that turned old scars into murals and long nights into a full-time hobby.
Your suspect talked about a gate that’s seen more speeches than weddings and still isn’t tired of tourists.
They said they liked cities that pulled down their walls and then put their secrets in basements with loud music.
new_york_city: They kept calling some place ‘the city that never sleeps’ as if insomnia was a tourist attraction.
Your thief asked if it’s true that yellow taxis there scream at each other in every language at once.
They mentioned skyscrapers so tall even pigeons have to take the elevator in their imagination.
warsaw: They asked me if I’d ever seen a capital rebuilt from ashes, stone by stubborn stone.
Your suspect talked about a river watched by a mermaid and a castle that refuses to retire.
They said they admired cities that fall, stand up again, and still manage to complain about tram schedules.
new_delhi: They smelled like dust, spices, and long flights, and asked if any city can be that loud and still hopeful.
Your thief wanted directions to a place where markets never really sleep and traffic plays its own percussion.
They joked that in this city even the cows look more confident crossing the street than most bankers.

banter: London streets drip, mumble and pretend they’ve seen worse.
I sleep under bridges tourists photograph from a distance.
Here, even the pigeons look like they’re late for work.
repeatLines: We already spoke, detective.
The fog hasn’t revealed anything new since.
Back again?
You must really like damp benches and old stories.
No new clues.
Just the same river, same stones, and slightly colder hands.
falseLeadLines: Even the rain knew you were in the wrong place.
Only your umbrella and your patience got tested.

banter: In Paris, even the trash has better posture than I do.
I see more broken hearts than broken bottles here, and that’s saying something.
The alleyways smell like smoke, perfume and people pretending they’re not lost.
repeatLines: We already talked, detective.
The only thing that changed is which café kicked me out.
Back so soon?
Romance moves faster than clues in this city.
No fresh secrets.
Just the same shadows and slightly louder arguments.
falseLeadLines: You followed the lights and forgot the trail.
Only tourists, poets, and people lying about both.

banter: Berlin streets wear their history on the walls and their hangovers in the morning.
I sleep where the city forgot to gentrify.
Some nights here last so long the day just apologises and waits.
repeatLines: We already covered this corner.
It still remembers more music than crime.
Back again?
Same graffiti, same faces, same missing thief.
No new whispers, detective.
Just the echo of bass lines and bad decisions.
falseLeadLines: You chased the wrong beat this time.
The suspect wasn’t in that crowd.
You just danced around the problem.

banter: New York sidewalks never sleep. They just change shoes.
I get pushed past by people who think time is money and I owe them both.
Here, the trash talks, the cabs swear, and the alleys remember everything.
repeatLines: Yeah, we already talked, detective.
Still the same chaos, still the same clue count.
Back again?
You’re starting to look like part of the scenery.
No update.
The city shouted a lot, but none of it was useful.
falseLeadLines: Just a million other problems on different corners.

banter: Warsaw streets have seen worse than me and still keep moving.
I sleep near walls that remember more than the people leaning on them.
This city rebuilds faster than some people learn.
repeatLines: We already talked.
No new faces, no new trouble on this corner.
Back again?
You’re more stubborn than the tram schedule.
Nothing new, detective.
If something shifted, I’d have felt it in the pavement.
falseLeadLines: Not your first mistake, probably not your last.
Like most promises shouted after midnight.
Just people trying to make rent and sense of things.

banter: In New Delhi, even the shadows feel crowded.
I sleep where the noise finally gets tired, which is never for long.
The streets here smell like spice, fuel and people who refuse to slow down.
repeatLines: We already spoke, detective.
Since then only the dust has moved.
Back again?
You must really like heat and bad odds.
No new clue.
Just the same traffic, same shouts and different excuses.
falseLeadLines: Loud mistake, easy to hear from here.
Like most cheap lanterns in a long night.
You only managed to chase the heat.
